classification.difficultyReason: Compare a supplied Pythagorean triple with the consecutive-side relationship imposed by the generation procedure.

content.prompt:
The following method produces Pythagorean triples: take an odd number as the length of one side, square it and subtract 1, then halve the result to obtain the second side. Add 1 to the second side to obtain the hypotenuse.

Not all Pythagorean triples can be produced in this way – an example is the triple $15,8,17$. Can you see why this triple does not fit the pattern?

answer.short: The method makes the hypotenuse 1 greater than the second side. Here the hypotenuse is 17, but neither 15 nor 8 is 16.
answer.worked: The second side and hypotenuse produced by the method differ by 1. For the given triple, the hypotenuse is 17, so the method would require a second side of 16. Neither other side is 16, so this triple cannot be produced by the method.
